download_for_offlineMusic overview
Music
“Music can change the world.” Ludwig van Beethoven
“When words fail, music speaks” Hans Christian Anderson
Our music curriculum ensures that all pupils are given opportunities to perform, listen to, review and evaluate music. We provide diverse opportunities for our children to perform and listen to music across historical periods, genres, styles, and traditions. Singing is the heartbeat of our music curriculum, acting as a form of personal expression that fosters creativity and self-belief. They not only learn to sing but also respectfully engage in creating and composing their own music. Our commitment to showcasing the works of great composers and musicians adds depth to their musical exploration. Through experimentation, improvisation, and the use of technology, we empower them to be musical creators. Our curriculum provides opportunities for all children to learn a musical instrument, fostering curiosity and a connection with music that goes beyond the theoretical. The inter-related dimensions of pitch, duration, dynamics, tempo, timbre, texture, structure are integral to our teaching. We dip in and out of the award winning 'Charanga' musical scheme, building cross curricular connections where possible, so that our music curriculum is engaging and meaningful for our children.
In our dedicated music room, Surrey Arts qualified Music Tutors guide our students through their rich musical journey. Moreover, we actively encourage children to showcase their talents, promoting community cohesion within and beyond the school. Through our music curriculum, we aim not only to cultivate musicians but also to inspire individuals who appreciate the beauty of music and its ability to positively impact the world around them

SEND and Safeguarding
Education and health services work closely together with parents to support children and young people with special educational needs and disabilities
At Cranmere Primary School we are proud to be an inclusive school where every child is valued and supported to achieve their full potential. We recognise that some children may need additional help at different times in their learning journey, and our dedicated Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) team works closely with pupils, families, and staff to provide the right support. Through tailored teaching, specialist interventions, and strong partnerships with external professionals, we aim to ensure that all children feel happy, confident, and able to thrive.
For further information about our Inclusion offer here at Cranmere, please watch this video:
/i/video/Inclusion_at_Cranmere.mp4
If you would like to find out more about our SEND provision, please contact our Inclusion Lead, Miss Hamilton, who will be happy to help.
Click this link to access further information about all the services available in Surrey for children and young people with special educational needs and/or disabilities (SEND) aged 0 to 25.

pageCache.text:
download_for_offlineArt overview
Art
Art is not what you see, but what you make others see.” Edgar Degas
At Cranmere Primary school, we seek to engage and challenge pupils to create their own works of art, by equipping them with the skills and knowledge they need. Through sharing the work of a range of artists from different cultures and genders, we seek to inspire curiosity in art and design and how these link to our history, reflecting and shaping our culture and the world around us. We encourage children to develop resilience when experimenting with a variety of media, working to create both two and three-dimensional pieces, developing and refining their skills as they progress. To express their own ideas through their art, whilst considering and respecting the opinions of others will encourage our children to be successful artists. Through art, we aim to develop self-belief and the courage to be creative.

Computing
‘Everybody in this country should learn how to program a computer because it teaches you how to think.’ Steve Jobs
Computing is a subject that allows us to connect, collaborate and create. We aim to inspire our children to become digital citizens; individuals responsible for how they use technology to interact with the world around them, that prepares our young people for life in a digital world, not just as passive users of technology, but active participants who create content, write programs and build systems’. Our computing curriculum aims to equip pupils with the foundations for understanding the ever-changing digital world in which they live by offering opportunities to gain knowledge and develop skills that will enable them to use, confidently and competently, computational thinking and creativity in the disciplines of Computer Science, Information Technology, Digital Literacy and Online Safety. Pupils will build a body of key foundational computing knowledge as they work through the curriculum, developing their creativity, resilience, problem solving, and critical thinking skills, developing a sense of curiosity about the world around them and to enable them to become responsible digital citizens.

Design & Technology
“Creativity is allowing yourself to make mistakes. Design is knowing which ones to keep.” Scott Adams
“Design is not for philosophy. It is for life” Issey Miyake
At Cranmere we recognise that Design Technology is an inspiring, rigorous and practical subject, which encourages children think and intervene creatively demonstrating their resilience and self-belief to solve problems both as individuals and members of a team. We nurture curiosity, creativity and imagination allowing our children to engage in the iterative process of design and make products that solve real and relevant problems within a variety of contexts. We aim to link their work to other areas of the curriculum ensuring they revisit and retrieve learning, cementing their understanding across a range of subjects including mathematics, PSHE and communication and language. Recognising that learning to cook is a crucial life skill we instil a love of cooking which will support our children to develop heathy eating habits, promote lifelong positive attitudes and enjoyment of good food and cooking. Our intent is that our children leave our care having developed a good base of foundation skills to perform everyday tasks confidently so they become global citizens who actively contribute to the creativity, culture, wealth and wellbeing of themselves and their community.

English
“Reading is the gateway for children that makes all other learning possible.” – Barack Obama
“One book, one pen, one child, and one teacher can change the world.” – Malala Yousafzai
At Cranmere, our English curriculum is designed to allow our children to develop into confident, creative writers, readers and communicators preparing them for later life as successful valuable and socially responsible citizens. We promote a positive attitude to reading by ensuring that this happens through a range of experiences and frequently, as well as celebrating our literary heritage. We nurture a positive climate for writing where our children take pride in their writing, can write clearly, imaginatively and for a range of audiences and contexts. At all times we inspire our children to be confident orators and use many avenues – debates, assemblies, productions - to further their learning across all areas of the curriculum. We believe that our children need to develop a solid and secure knowledge in all aspects of Literacy, which is built on as they progress through our school, and in doing so we believe that these skills are crucial to a high-quality education in all their learning. At Cranmere we passionately ‘promote high standards of literacy by equipping pupils with a strong command of the spoken and written word, and to develop their love of literature through widespread reading for enjoyment.' (National Curriculum 2014)
To support and develop children's love for reading, we have created a series of 'recommended reads' for every year group. To find out more about each year group's list, please take a look at the linked documents on this page.
